# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 30 (Bu-Vb Pc30)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Rahonisajja Sikkhāpada* constitutes the thirtieth *pācittiya* training rule of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The core rule formulated in the Pātimokkha stipulates an offense of expiation for any monk who sits down in private, one-on-one, with a Buddhist nun (*yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhuniyā saddhiṁ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṁ kappeyya pācittiyaṁ*) [Dutt 1924; SuttaCentral]. According to the rule's non-offense clause (*anāpatti*), it is not considered an infraction if the monk remains standing rather than sitting down, a distinction shared with related regulations such as Pācittiya 44 and 45 and corroborated by the casuistry of Aniyata 1 and 2 [Hüsken 1997]. In the commentary tradition, Buddhaghosa's *Samantapāsādikā* does not provide an independent exposition for Pācittiya 30, instead passing over it with a cross-reference to other Vinaya ordinances [Hüsken 1997].
Curated parallels recorded by SuttaCentral include the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Pc 30) and *Parivāra* (Pc 30), along with matching Vinaya rules in the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, and Dharmaguptaka recensions in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan, as well as corresponding rules for nuns (*Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*) across several traditions [SuttaCentral]. At the passage level, SuttaCentral identifies shared textual structures with Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 44, Pācittiya 45, Aniyata 1, and Aniyata 2 [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus strongly corroborates these connections through internal Pali reuse data, showing substantial formulaic overlap especially with Pācittiya 45 (§1.4–2.3.8) and Pācittiya 44 (§1.5–1.13.1), along with Pācittiya 46, 43, and Aniyata 2 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also establishes automated cross-language alignments with Tibetan Prātimokṣa commentaries (such as the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* and *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya*) and Sanskrit Vinaya texts including the *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* and *Prātimokṣasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
